title: Regenerate must clear Batch billing attributes once M11 telemetry lands
description:
\`_regenerate_admin_job\` (cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py, from auritus-907209)
REMOVEs every ephemeral attribute that \`_claim_job\`/\`_mark_done\`/\`_mark_failed\`
can write, so a regenerated job starts clean. It predates M11's batch billing
telemetry story (auritus-d43efe / auritus-bb0dac), which adds
\`batch_created_at\`, \`batch_started_at\`, \`batch_stopped_at\`,
\`container_seconds\`, \`provisioning_seconds\`, \`billed_seconds\`,
\`instance_type\`, and later cost fields to job records.

None of those are in the regenerate REMOVE list. Once M11 lands, regenerating
a job that previously ran on Batch will keep its old billing/cost attributes
on the reset record -- a job now genuinely pending would still show a stale
GPU cost from its prior run until it completes again (or forever, if it's
picked up locally instead).

Extend \`_regenerate_admin_job\`'s REMOVE clause to cover the M11 attributes
when that epic's job-record schema exists. Add a regression scenario to
\`features/job_regeneration.feature\` asserting a regenerated job has no
leftover billing attributes.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implemented on fix/regenerate-clears-billing-attrs, merged to develop. Extended _regenerate_admin_job's and _retry_admin_job's REMOVE clauses with every billing/telemetry attribute (gpu_cost_usd, platform_cost_usd, cost_rate_usd_per_hour, rate_card_version, avoided_cost_usd, avoided_cost_basis, batch_created_at/started_at/stopped_at, instance_type, container_seconds, provisioning_seconds, billed_seconds) plus all three idempotency flags (platform_cost_rolled_up, gpu_cost_rolled_up, backend_timing_rolled_up). Agent independently found and fixed the identical gap in _retry_admin_job that I'd only asked it to check for, correctly reasoning that a stuck-claimed job could carry batch_telemetry flags from before it got stuck. Confirmed the idempotency-flag omission was a real under-counting bug, not just stale-data cosmetics: without clearing those flags, a regenerated/retried job's real cost on its next completion would be silently skipped by the rollup guards. Independently re-verified: reverted the fix myself and confirmed both new scenarios genuinely fail. Full suite green: black/ruff, pytest (72 passed), behave (30 features, 118 scenarios).
